content.text:
# Muxy Test Practices Survey (as of `03a6420`, 2026-08-12)

Scope: `~/dev/muxy/Tests/` (single directory, single test target). No new XCUITest target, no snapshot library, no separate integration-test target was found — everything lives in one Swift Testing target. 334 test files, ~64,500 lines, 3,297 `@Test` functions. For scale, 158 commits ago (≈2026-06-24, `e5e9b83`) there were 184 test files — the suite has grown ~1.8x since your last known state.

## 1. Directory/target structure

- One SPM test target, `MuxyTests` (`Package.swift:118-149`), depending on almost every module: `Muxy`, `MuxyShared`, `MuxyServer`, `MuxySessionProtocol`, `MuxyExtensionHost`, `MuxyHookKit`, plus `Yams`. No `MuxyUITests`, no `MuxySessionTests`, no per-module test targets — everything is one flat target that mirrors the app's internal folder layout instead of the package's module boundaries.
- `Tests/MuxyTests/` mirrors `Muxy/`'s own subtree almost 1:1: `Git/`, `Models/<Feature>/`, `Services/<Feature>/`, `Views/<Feature>/`, `Remote/`, `Utilities/`, `Theme/`, plus one cross-cutting `Support/` folder.
- Naming convention: `<TypeUnderTest>Tests.swift`, one file per unit under test, e.g. `Tests/MuxyTests/Services/Git/GitRepositoryCheckCoordinatorTests.swift` tests `GitRepositoryCheckCoordinator`. Very fine-grained — e.g. `GitWorktreeServiceAddTests.swift` and `GitWorktreeServiceRemoveTests.swift` split the two operations of one service into separate files.
- No XCUITest target exists anywhere in the repo (`GhosttyKit`, `MuxyExtensionHost`, etc. also have no tests of their own outside `MuxyTests`).

## 2. Test infrastructure/helpers

`Tests/MuxyTests/Support/` (7 files) is genuinely shared, but it's thin and single-purpose per file — there is no general-purpose `TestSupport` module or umbrella "TestKit":

- `RepositoryRoot.swift` — walks up from `#filePath` to find `Package.swift`, used to locate build products (`.build/debug/muxy-session`) from tests.
- `SessionDaemonHarness.swift` (239 lines) — a full end-to-end harness: spawns the real `muxy-session` daemon binary, speaks the real Unix-socket wire protocol (`SessionFrame`/`SessionFrameDecoder`), exposes `start()/stop()`, `attachRequest(...)`, `runAttachClient(...)`. This is the most substantial shared helper in the repo.
- `MuxyAPIEnvironment.swift` — reusable stub persistence classes (`ProjectGroupPersistenceStub`, `ProjectManagementPersistenceStub`, etc.) plus a `ProjectManagementEnvironment` struct that wires up a whole `AppState`/`ProjectStore`/`WorktreeStore`/`ProjectGroupStore` graph for `MuxyAPI` tests.
- `InMemoryWorkspaceContextSink.swift`, `TerminalViewRemovingTestDefaults.swift`, `ExtensionManifestFixture.swift`, `LocalizationTestSupport.swift` — small, single-protocol fakes/builders.

**Fixture code is still heavily duplicated per-file** despite `Support/` existing — this is the single clearest gap:
- A `private struct TempGitRepo` (init a real git repo in a temp dir, `run`/`runCapturing`/`commit` helpers) is independently reimplemented in `Git/GitWorktreeServiceAddTests.swift:57-121`, `Git/GitWorktreeServiceRemoveTests.swift`, and `Git/GitRepositoryServiceNewAPIsTests.swift:470+` — three near-identical but subtly different copies (different temp-dir prefixes, one adds `createBareRemote()`/`isSameDirectory()`).
- A `private final class StubURLProtocol: URLProtocol` (network mocking) is duplicated in `Services/Extensions/ExtensionHTTPClientTests.swift:193-211`, `Services/Extensions/ExtensionMarketplaceServiceTests.swift`, and `Views/Components/Icons/ExtensionRemoteIconCacheTests.swift`.
- 74 files independently call `FileManager.default.temporaryDirectory.appendingPathComponent("...\(UUID().uuidString)")`; 11 files each define their own private `makeTempDir()`/`temporaryDirectory()`/`tempDirectory()` helper (e.g. `Services/FileSystem/WorkspaceFileServiceTests.swift` defines it three separate times at lines 131, 444, 779 within the same file).

Takeaway for Workroom: Muxy's `Support/` pattern (one file per cross-cutting concern) is worth adopting, but the git-fixture-repo and URL-mock duplication is a known-bad pattern you can improve on rather than copy.

## 3. How UI is tested — the "never run the app" policy is unchanged

`CLAUDE.md:33` still states explicitly: **"Never run the app. User will run and test visually."** This is current policy, not stale. `CONTRIBUTING.md` has no UI-testing section at all. There is no XCUITest target, no `XCUIApplication` reference anywhere in the repo, and no snapshot-testing dependency in `Package.resolved` (only `Sparkle`, `Yams`, `sentry-cocoa`).

Instead, UI is tested at the unit level by instantiating real AppKit/SwiftUI objects off-screen and asserting on their structure/geometry — no rendering pipeline, no screenshot comparison:
- **AppKit view-tree assertions**: `Views/QuickTerminal/QuickTerminalContentViewTests.swift:9-37` builds a real `QuickTerminalContentView(frame:)`, calls `.layout()`, then asserts on `subviews`, z-order (`firstIndex(of:)`), `NSVisualEffectView.material`, `layer?.backgroundColor?.alpha`.
- **SwiftUI via `NSHostingView` + forced layout**, no window, no run loop: `Views/Extensions/ExtensionConsentDialogTests.swift:36-51` — `let hostingView = NSHostingView(rootView: view); hostingView.layoutSubtreeIfNeeded(); #expect(hostingView.fittingSize.height <= 620)`. This is the closest thing to "rendering" and it's purely deterministic layout math, never a pixel comparison.
- **Accessibility identifiers as a lookup seam**, not an XCUITest seam: `Muxy/Views/QuickTerminal/QuickTerminalContentView.swift:312` etc. call `setAccessibilityIdentifier(...)` on a handful of AppKit views; the corresponding test (`QuickTerminalContentViewTests.swift:187,195`) walks `subviews` matching `.accessibilityIdentifier()` to find them programmatically. This is a very limited, ad hoc pattern (5 call sites in one source file) — not a systematic testability convention.
- Pure "policy" objects (`OverlayEscapeDecision`, `MainWindowModalPolicy` in `Views/MainWindowTests.swift:4-46`) are extracted so view logic can be tested without any view at all.

Conclusion for topic 3: the policy is confirmed unchanged — no XCUITest, no "run the app" testing was added in the 158-commit window.

## 4. Concurrency/async testing

Swift Testing's `async`/`await` is used pervasively (3,297 `@Test`s, most `async throws`), and there's a clear, deliberate pattern for deterministic race testing via **private `actor` gates** that hand out `CheckedContinuation`s to control interleaving instead of sleeping and hoping:

- `Services/Git/GitRepositoryCheckCoordinatorTests.swift:148-211` — `private actor GitRepositoryCheckProbe` tracks `activePaths`, exposes `waitForActiveChecks(_ target: Int) async` (suspends until N concurrent calls are in-flight) and `releaseAll()`. Tests do:
  ```swift
  async let checkResults = results(for: repositories, coordinator: coordinator)
  await probe.waitForActiveChecks(2)
  await probe.releaseAll()
  #expect(await probe.maximumActiveCheckCount == 2)
  ```
  This lets them assert exact concurrency caps (`limitsConcurrentChecks`, `remoteChecksDoNotStarveLocalChecks`) without timing flakiness. It also exercises `withTaskCancellationHandler` to verify cancelled probes are counted.
- The same "actor gate" idiom recurs independently in `Services/MuxyAPI/MuxyAPIProjectDeleteTests.swift:393` (`ProjectRemovalTestGate`), `Services/Extensions/ExtensionCommandExecutorTests.swift:790` (`AuthorizationFailureGate`), `Services/Project/WorktreeStoreTests.swift:813` (`WorktreeMutationTestGate`), `Services/Voice/ComposerVoiceStateTests.swift:151` (`PermissionGate`), `Services/AI/ProviderDiscoveryServiceTests.swift:330,339` (`ProbeSequence`/`ProbeGate`), `Services/AI/RepositoryAIActionsServiceTests.swift:400,418`, `Services/ProjectPicker/ProjectPickerWorkflowTests.swift:186,206` — 11 hand-rolled actors total, each private to its file (another duplication opportunity, but each is a small variation, not a copy-paste).
- `@Suite(..., .serialized)` is applied to 33 suites specifically where shared static/singleton state (UserDefaults suites, stores, the session daemon) would otherwise race under Swift Testing's default parallel execution — e.g. `Services/Session/SessionDaemonEndToEndTests.swift:8` combines `.serialized` with `.enabled(if: SessionDaemonHarness.binaryURL != nil)` to skip gracefully when the debug binary hasn't been built.
- `@Suite(..., .timeLimit(.minutes(1)))` used twice (`Services/AgentDetection/AgentProcessExitWatcherTests.swift:6`, `Services/Git/GitRepositoryCheckCoordinatorTests.swift:6`) as a deadlock/hang guard on suites that wait on real OS processes or continuations.
- `@MainActor` appears on 175 test files/suites (structs/classes annotated at suite level), matching production code's `@MainActor` isolation rather than fighting it.
- 32 files use `@unchecked Sendable` on test doubles as a pragmatic escape hatch under Swift 6's strict concurrency (tools-version 6.0 in `Package.swift:1`), rather than a systematic `Sendable`-safe design for every stub.
- No `confirmation()` API usage found (Swift Testing's built-in async-event-confirmation helper) — they consistently prefer their own actor-gate idiom over that stdlib feature.

## 5. External dependency isolation (shell-outs, filesystem, network)

Mixed strategy — **real ephemeral resources for git/subprocess/socket-level tests, protocol-based fakes for everything else**:

- **Git**: never mocked. Every git test spins up a real repo via `/usr/bin/env git` in `FileManager.default.temporaryDirectory` and asserts on real `git` output (`Git/GitWorktreeServiceAddTests.swift:101-119`). `Git/GitProcessRunnerTimeoutTests.swift:8-27` even exercises real process timeout/kill behavior: `try await GitProcessRunner.runGit(..., arguments: ["-c", "alias.wait=!sleep 10 &", "wait"], timeout: 0.5)` expecting `GitProcessError.self` to throw.
- **Pure logic around shell-outs is isolated via closure injection**, not filesystem mocking: `Git/GitProcessRunnerCredentialHelperTests.swift:9-11` — `GitProcessRunner.gitHubCredentialHelperArgs { _ in nil }` injects the "where is `gh`" resolver as a closure so arg-building logic is tested with zero filesystem/process access.
- **Session daemon / IPC**: real subprocess + real Unix domain socket, no mocking at all — `Support/SessionDaemonHarness.swift` launches the actual `muxy-session` binary from `.build/debug/`, and `SessionTestConnection` does raw `socket()/connect()/read()/write()` against `AF_UNIX`. Tests are skipped (not failed) via `.enabled(if: SessionDaemonHarness.binaryURL != nil)` when the binary isn't built.
- **Filesystem** is abstracted behind protocols where it matters for determinism: `Muxy/Services/ProjectPicker/ProjectPickerPathService.swift:55-59` defines `protocol ProjectPickerFileSystem: Sendable` with a real `FileManagerProjectPickerFileSystem` implementation; tests use in-memory fakes (`CountingProjectPickerFileSystem`, `ProjectPickerPathServiceFileSystemStub` in `Services/ProjectPicker/ProjectPickerPathServiceTests.swift:142-163`) that assert call counts and return canned entries with zero disk I/O.
- **Network** is mocked via a hand-rolled `URLProtocol` subclass (`private final class StubURLProtocol: URLProtocol`, duplicated in 3 files) registered per-test with a static `handler` closure — no third-party HTTP mocking library.
- The codebase has a broad protocol-seam convention for DI generally: 15+ `...Persisting`/`...Operating`/`...Providing`/`...FileSystem` protocols in `Muxy/Services/` (e.g. `ProjectPersisting`, `WorktreePersisting`, `RepositoryAIGitOperating`, `RemoteFileOps`), each with a production `FileManager`/real implementation and test stubs — this is the backbone that makes most non-git/non-daemon tests fast and hermetic.
- **Application Support isolation** (new since your last survey, PR #899, 2026-07-14): `Muxy/Services/Persistence/JSONFilePersistence.swift:4-7` detects test processes via `ProcessInfo.processInfo.processName` (`"swiftpm-testing-helper"`, `"xctest"`, or suffix `"Tests"`) and redirects `appSupportDirectory()` to an isolated temp path (`resolvedAppSupportDirectory()`, lines 29-38), honoring `MUXY_TEST_APPLICATION_SUPPORT_DIRECTORY` if set. `scripts/run-tests-isolated.sh` sets both `CFFIXED_USER_HOME` and that env var to a fresh `mktemp -d` before running `swift test`, and cleans up via `trap cleanup EXIT INT TERM`. There's even a meta-test guarding this: `Tests/MuxyTests/Utilities/TestIsolationScriptTests.swift:43-51` reads `scripts/checks.sh`/`scripts/coverage.sh` source and asserts they still invoke `run-tests-isolated.sh` — a regression guard against someone accidentally removing the isolation wrapper.

## 6. Snapshot/visual testing

None. No `swift-snapshot-testing` or similar dependency in `Package.resolved` or `Package.swift`. No image-comparison code anywhere in `Tests/`. This has not changed since before the 158-commit gap. Visual verification, per `CLAUDE.md`, is entirely manual ("User will run and test visually").

## 7. Test data/fixtures for git/VCS and file-tree scenarios

- Git fixtures: three independent `TempGitRepo` implementations (see §2) create real repos with `git init -q -b main`, `git config user.email/user.name/commit.gpgsign=false`, then build history via `commit(file:contents:message:)`. `Git/GitRepositoryServiceNewAPIsTests.swift` extends this with `createBareRemote()` and `setRemoteHEAD`/`detachRemoteHEAD` to test fetch/fast-forward against a real bare remote — i.e. full local git plumbing, no network.
- File-tree fixtures: no shared builder; each file's private `makeTempDir()` creates a throwaway directory tree (e.g. `Services/FileSystem/WorkspaceFileServiceTests.swift`, `Remote/RemoteServerDelegateFilesTests.swift:239`) and manually writes files with `Data(...).write(to:)`.
- `Support/ExtensionManifestFixture.swift:3-32` is the one proper fixture *builder*: converts a flat test-friendly manifest string into a real `package.json` on disk (`write(flatManifest:to:)`), used across extension tests instead of hand-writing JSON in each file.
- `Support/LocalizationTestSupport.swift:6-57` builds a full fake `.bundle`/`.lproj` structure on disk plus an isolated `UserDefaults(suiteName:)` — a good example of a fixture that composes filesystem + UserDefaults isolation in one reusable call.

# Muxy Test Practices Survey (as of `03a6420`, 2026-08-12)

Scope: `~/dev/muxy/Tests/` (single directory, single test target). No new XCUITest target, no snapshot library, no separate integration-test target was found — everything lives in one Swift Testing target. 334 test files, ~64,500 lines, 3,297 `@Test` functions. For scale, 158 commits ago (≈2026-06-24, `e5e9b83`) there were 184 test files — the suite has grown ~1.8x since your last known state.

## 1. Directory/target structure

- One SPM test target, `MuxyTests` (`Package.swift:118-149`), depending on almost every module: `Muxy`, `MuxyShared`, `MuxyServer`, `MuxySessionProtocol`, `MuxyExtensionHost`, `MuxyHookKit`, plus `Yams`. No `MuxyUITests`, no `MuxySessionTests`, no per-module test targets — everything is one flat target that mirrors the app's internal folder layout instead of the package's module boundaries.
- `Tests/MuxyTests/` mirrors `Muxy/`'s own subtree almost 1:1: `Git/`, `Models/<Feature>/`, `Services/<Feature>/`, `Views/<Feature>/`, `Remote/`, `Utilities/`, `Theme/`, plus one cross-cutting `Support/` folder.
- Naming convention: `<TypeUnderTest>Tests.swift`, one file per unit under test, e.g. `Tests/MuxyTests/Services/Git/GitRepositoryCheckCoordinatorTests.swift` tests `GitRepositoryCheckCoordinator`. Very fine-grained — e.g. `GitWorktreeServiceAddTests.swift` and `GitWorktreeServiceRemoveTests.swift` split the two operations of one service into separate files.
- No XCUITest target exists anywhere in the repo (`GhosttyKit`, `MuxyExtensionHost`, etc. also have no tests of their own outside `MuxyTests`).

## 2. Test infrastructure/helpers

`Tests/MuxyTests/Support/` (7 files) is genuinely shared, but it's thin and single-purpose per file — there is no general-purpose `TestSupport` module or umbrella "TestKit":

- `RepositoryRoot.swift` — walks up from `#filePath` to find `Package.swift`, used to locate build products (`.build/debug/muxy-session`) from tests.
- `SessionDaemonHarness.swift` (239 lines) — a full end-to-end harness: spawns the real `muxy-session` daemon binary, speaks the real Unix-socket wire protocol (`SessionFrame`/`SessionFrameDecoder`), exposes `start()/stop()`, `attachRequest(...)`, `runAttachClient(...)`. This is the most substantial shared helper in the repo.
- `MuxyAPIEnvironment.swift` — reusable stub persistence classes (`ProjectGroupPersistenceStub`, `ProjectManagementPersistenceStub`, etc.) plus a `ProjectManagementEnvironment` struct that wires up a whole `AppState`/`ProjectStore`/`WorktreeStore`/`ProjectGroupStore` graph for `MuxyAPI` tests.
- `InMemoryWorkspaceContextSink.swift`, `TerminalViewRemovingTestDefaults.swift`, `ExtensionManifestFixture.swift`, `LocalizationTestSupport.swift` — small, single-protocol fakes/builders.

**Fixture code is still heavily duplicated per-file** despite `Support/` existing — this is the single clearest gap:
- A `private struct TempGitRepo` (init a real git repo in a temp dir, `run`/`runCapturing`/`commit` helpers) is independently reimplemented in `Git/GitWorktreeServiceAddTests.swift:57-121`, `Git/GitWorktreeServiceRemoveTests.swift`, and `Git/GitRepositoryServiceNewAPIsTests.swift:470+` — three near-identical but subtly different copies (different temp-dir prefixes, one adds `createBareRemote()`/`isSameDirectory()`).
- A `private final class StubURLProtocol: URLProtocol` (network mocking) is duplicated in `Services/Extensions/ExtensionHTTPClientTests.swift:193-211`, `Services/Extensions/ExtensionMarketplaceServiceTests.swift`, and `Views/Components/Icons/ExtensionRemoteIconCacheTests.swift`.
- 74 files independently call `FileManager.default.temporaryDirectory.appendingPathComponent("...\(UUID().uuidString)")`; 11 files each define their own private `makeTempDir()`/`temporaryDirectory()`/`tempDirectory()` helper (e.g. `Services/FileSystem/WorkspaceFileServiceTests.swift` defines it three separate times at lines 131, 444, 779 within the same file).

Takeaway for Workroom: Muxy's `Support/` pattern (one file per cross-cutting concern) is worth adopting, but the git-fixture-repo and URL-mock duplication is a known-bad pattern you can improve on rather than copy.

## 3. How UI is tested — the "never run the app" policy is unchanged

`CLAUDE.md:33` still states explicitly: **"Never run the app. User will run and test visually."** This is current policy, not stale. `CONTRIBUTING.md` has no UI-testing section at all. There is no XCUITest target, no `XCUIApplication` reference anywhere in the repo, and no snapshot-testing dependency in `Package.resolved` (only `Sparkle`, `Yams`, `sentry-cocoa`).

Instead, UI is tested at the unit level by instantiating real AppKit/SwiftUI objects off-screen and asserting on their structure/geometry — no rendering pipeline, no screenshot comparison:
- **AppKit view-tree assertions**: `Views/QuickTerminal/QuickTerminalContentViewTests.swift:9-37` builds a real `QuickTerminalContentView(frame:)`, calls `.layout()`, then asserts on `subviews`, z-order (`firstIndex(of:)`), `NSVisualEffectView.material`, `layer?.backgroundColor?.alpha`.
- **SwiftUI via `NSHostingView` + forced layout**, no window, no run loop: `Views/Extensions/ExtensionConsentDialogTests.swift:36-51` — `let hostingView = NSHostingView(rootView: view); hostingView.layoutSubtreeIfNeeded(); #expect(hostingView.fittingSize.height <= 620)`. This is the closest thing to "rendering" and it's purely deterministic layout math, never a pixel comparison.
- **Accessibility identifiers as a lookup seam**, not an XCUITest seam: `Muxy/Views/QuickTerminal/QuickTerminalContentView.swift:312` etc. call `setAccessibilityIdentifier(...)` on a handful of AppKit views; the corresponding test (`QuickTerminalContentViewTests.swift:187,195`) walks `subviews` matching `.accessibilityIdentifier()` to find them programmatically. This is a very limited, ad hoc pattern (5 call sites in one source file) — not a systematic testability convention.
- Pure "policy" objects (`OverlayEscapeDecision`, `MainWindowModalPolicy` in `Views/MainWindowTests.swift:4-46`) are extracted so view logic can be tested without any view at all.

Conclusion for topic 3: the policy is confirmed unchanged — no XCUITest, no "run the app" testing was added in the 158-commit window.

Swift Testing's `async`/`await` is used pervasively (3,297 `@Test`s, most `async throws`), and there's a clear, deliberate pattern for deterministic race testing via **private `actor` gates** that hand out `CheckedContinuation`s to control interleaving instead of sleeping and hoping:

- `Services/Git/GitRepositoryCheckCoordinatorTests.swift:148-211` — `private actor GitRepositoryCheckProbe` tracks `activePaths`, exposes `waitForActiveChecks(_ target: Int) async` (suspends until N concurrent calls are in-flight) and `releaseAll()`. Tests do:
  ```swift
  async let checkResults = results(for: repositories, coordinator: coordinator)
  await probe.waitForActiveChecks(2)
  await probe.releaseAll()
  #expect(await probe.maximumActiveCheckCount == 2)
  ```

- `@Suite(..., .serialized)` is applied to 33 suites specifically where shared static/singleton state (UserDefaults suites, stores, the session daemon) would otherwise race under Swift Testing's default parallel execution — e.g. `Services/Session/SessionDaemonEndToEndTests.swift:8` combines `.serialized` with `.enabled(if: SessionDaemonHarness.binaryURL != nil)` to skip gracefully when the debug binary hasn't been built.
- `@Suite(..., .timeLimit(.minutes(1)))` used twice (`Services/AgentDetection/AgentProcessExitWatcherTests.swift:6`, `Services/Git/GitRepositoryCheckCoordinatorTests.swift:6`) as a deadlock/hang guard on suites that wait on real OS processes or continuations.
- `@MainActor` appears on 175 test files/suites (structs/classes annotated at suite level), matching production code's `@MainActor` isolation rather than fighting it.
- 32 files use `@unchecked Sendable` on test doubles as a pragmatic escape hatch under Swift 6's strict concurrency (tools-version 6.0 in `Package.swift:1`), rather than a systematic `Sendable`-safe design for every stub.
- No `confirmation()` API usage found (Swift Testing's built-in async-event-confirmation helper) — they consistently prefer their own actor-gate idiom over that stdlib feature.

## 5. External dependency isolation (shell-outs, filesystem, network)

Mixed strategy — **real ephemeral resources for git/subprocess/socket-level tests, protocol-based fakes for everything else**:

- **Git**: never mocked. Every git test spins up a real repo via `/usr/bin/env git` in `FileManager.default.temporaryDirectory` and asserts on real `git` output (`Git/GitWorktreeServiceAddTests.swift:101-119`). `Git/GitProcessRunnerTimeoutTests.swift:8-27` even exercises real process timeout/kill behavior: `try await GitProcessRunner.runGit(..., arguments: ["-c", "alias.wait=!sleep 10 &", "wait"], timeout: 0.5)` expecting `GitProcessError.self` to throw.

- **Actor-gate deterministic concurrency testing** for the new `GitRepositoryCheckCoordinator` (PR #948, 2026-07-29) — `GitRepositoryCheckProbe` (§4) is a recent, well-crafted example of the pattern, worth using as the reference implementation if you introduce this technique in Workroom.

1. **Production-code test-process detection + isolated storage** (`MuxyFileStorage.isTestProcess`, `Muxy/Services/Persistence/JSONFilePersistence.swift:4-7,29-38`) plus a `run-tests-isolated.sh`-style wrapper — cheap, high-leverage, prevents test runs from touching real `~/Library/Application Support`.
2. **Actor-gate pattern for deterministic concurrency tests** (`GitRepositoryCheckProbe`, `Tests/MuxyTests/Services/Git/GitRepositoryCheckCoordinatorTests.swift:148-211`) — far more reliable than `Task.sleep`-based race tests.
3. **`NSHostingView` + `layoutSubtreeIfNeeded()` + `fittingSize` assertions** (`ExtensionConsentDialogTests.swift:36-51`) as a no-XCUITest, no-snapshot way to test SwiftUI layout behavior.
4. **Meta-test that greps your own CI/check scripts** (`TestIsolationScriptTests.swift:43-51`) to guard invariants about how tests are invoked.
5. **Closure-injected external-tool resolvers** (`GitProcessRunner.gitHubCredentialHelperArgs { _ in nil }`) for testing argument-building logic without touching the filesystem/PATH.
6. What to avoid copying: the per-file `TempGitRepo`/`StubURLProtocol`/`makeTempDir()` duplication — Workroom could get the same coverage with less maintenance by extracting one shared `TestSupport`-style git-fixture and URL-mock helper from day one, something Muxy itself hasn't done despite having a `Support/` folder.

content.text:
# Workroom (`macapp`) Test Practices Survey

## 1. Directory/target structure

Three test surfaces, all defined in `macapp/project.yml`:

- **`WorkroomAppTests`** (`type: bundle.unit-test`) — the unit/integration tier. `project.yml:280-300`ish: host-based via `TEST_HOST`/`BUNDLE_LOADER` pointed explicitly at `Workroom Dev.app` (XcodeGen's name-derived default is wrong here), so `@testable import Workroom` sees internals. Wired into the `WorkroomApp` scheme's `test:` action → this is what `make app-test` runs.
- **`WorkroomAppUITests`** (`type: bundle.ui-testing`) — XCUITest tier, deliberately kept **out** of the `WorkroomApp` scheme and given its **own** `WorkroomAppUITests` scheme, so `make app-test` never launches a GUI session. Run via `make app-uitest`.
- **`Tests/run-supervisor/`** — a hand-rolled Python integration test (`test_supervisor.py` + `fakeserver.py`, no pytest), for the run-command supervisor shell script, run via `make app-test-supervisor`.
- Plus two dependency-free `sh` test scripts (`Scripts/build-helper_test.sh`, `Scripts/channel-helper_test.sh`) run via `make app-test-scripts`.

Scale: **147 files / ~2,263 `func test*` methods** under `WorkroomAppTests`, **37 files / 191 methods** under `WorkroomAppUITests`. Both directories are **flat** — one file per feature/bug, no subfolder hierarchy (no `Core/`, `Views/`, `Models/` mirroring of the app's source tree). Naming convention is consistently `<Subject>Tests.swift` (unit) / `<Feature>UITests.swift` (UI), often named after the regression/issue it guards (e.g. `AppStoreDeleteRaceTests`, `WORKROOM-2B`/`2T` referenced in comments for hang regressions) rather than after a class 1:1.

The only subdirectory is `WorkroomAppTests/Support/` containing exactly two files: `Settle.swift` (a shared helper, see §4) and its own `SettleTests.swift`.

## 2. Test infrastructure/helpers

There is **no `TestKit`/shared-mocks package**. Two very different situations exist side by side:

- **One shared cross-cutting helper**: `WorkroomAppTests/Support/Settle.swift` — an `XCTestCase` extension providing a run-loop-pumping "settle" waiter, used by 7 files (`AgentResumeCoordinatorTests`, `ChangedFileRowInvalidationTests`, `HistoryRowInvalidationTests`, `DiffViewerLazyRenderingTests`, `RunCommandTests`, `RemoteStateModelTests`, `ChangedFileOpenTests`).
- **Everything else is duplicated per file.** DI protocols exist in production code (`VCSProviding`, `VCSWriting`, `StatusCommandRunning`, `AgentRunning`, `ReleasesFetching`, `WorkroomCLIProtocol`, `Trashing`, `SystemNotifying`), but their test doubles are re-implemented privately, file by file, with no shared library:
  - `WorkroomAppTests/BranchResolverTests.swift:7` — `private struct StubProvider: VCSProviding`
  - `WorkroomAppTests/HistoryModelTests.swift:18` — `private struct FakeProvider: VCSProviding`
  - `WorkroomAppTests/DiffResolverTests.swift:9`, `DiffResolverFileContentTests.swift:14`, `DiffResolverOldFileContentTests.swift:16` — three near-identical `VCSProviding` stubs (`StubDiffProvider`, `StubContentProvider`, `StubOldContentProvider`)
  - `WorkroomAppTests/WorkroomStatusResolverTests.swift:7`, `RustJJProviderRunTests.swift:6`, `FileTreeTests.swift:266`, `WorkroomStatusTests.swift:950` — four separate `StatusCommandRunning` stubs (`MockStatusRunner`, `StubRunner` ×2, `StubPRRunner`)
  - `AgentRunnerTests.swift:185` (`FakeExecutor`), `TerminalAgentManagerTests.swift:251` (`FakeAgentRunner`), `AppStoreAddProjectTests.swift:9` (`FakeWorkroomCLI`), `AppStoreDeleteProjectTests.swift:251` (`FakeTrasher`), `WhatsNewServiceTests.swift:7` (`FakeReleases`), `RemoteStateModelTests.swift:783` (`StubWriter: VCSWriting`).
  - Similarly, ~20 files independently define their own `private func tempDir()` (e.g. `GitGraphTests.swift:28`, `VCSRemoteIntegrationTests.swift:67`, `VCSProviderConformanceTests.swift:466`, `WorkroomStatusIntegrationTests.swift:40`) and their own `gitRepo`/`jjRepo` builders — no shared fixture factory.

This is a clear duplication gap worth flagging for Muxy comparison: DI seams are good, but there's no `Fakes.swift`/`TestSupport` module consolidating the `VCSProviding`/`StatusCommandRunning` stubs that recur across a dozen files.

## 3. XCUITest usage

**Fixture flag mechanism** — `WorkroomApp/Core/UITestFixture.swift` (the app-side seam, ~1000 lines). Launched with `-WorkroomUITestFixture 1`; gated `#if DEBUG` so it's inert in release builds (`UITestFixture.swift:34-40`). Dozens of additional `-WorkroomUITest*` launch args layer on top to select scenarios deterministically (`-WorkroomUITestJJProject 1`, `-WorkroomUITestManyCommits <n>`, `-WorkroomUITestSyncState <name>`, `-WorkroomUITestConflict 1`, `-WorkroomUITestGitWorkroom 1`, etc. — see `UITestFixture.swift:87-378`). Each XCUITest file builds its own `launchedApp()` helper, e.g.:

```swift
// WorkroomAppUITests/ActivityBarUITests.swift:13-20
private func launchedApp() -> XCUIApplication {
  let app = XCUIApplication()
  app.launchArguments += ["-WorkroomUITestFixture", "1"]
  app.launchArguments += ["-ApplePersistenceIgnoreState", "YES"]
  app.launch()
  app.activate()
  return app
}
```
33 of the 37 UI test files independently re-declare `launchedApp()`/`waitExists()` (confirmed by grep) — the same duplication pattern as the unit-test mocks, just for UI-test scaffolding instead of a shared XCUITest base class.

**Accessibility identifiers**: fixture-only ids, gated the same way, e.g. `activitySection.<rawValue>`, `inspector.header.<title>`, `sidebar.project.<name>`, `terminal.surface` (`GhosttySurfaceView.swift:1106-1108`: `override func accessibilityIdentifier() -> String { UITestFixture.isActive ? "terminal.surface" : super... }`).

**Terminal/Metal content assertion** — since libghostty renders through Metal with no text layer, `GhosttySurfaceView.swift` overrides `accessibilityValue()`/`accessibilitySelectedText()`/`accessibilityPlaceholderValue()` to expose `readText(tag: GHOSTTY_POINT_VIEWPORT)` (project memory's "fixture-only accessibilityValue pattern"), gated by:

```swift
// GhosttySurfaceView.swift:1060-1062
private var accessibilityContentEnabled: Bool {
  UITestFixture.isActive || NSWorkspace.shared.isVoiceOverEnabled
}
```
`readText(tag:)` (`GhosttySurfaceView.swift:845`) is the low-level libghostty read; `readFullSurface()` (`:866`) and `readCommandRegion(maxBytes:)` (`:822`) wrap it for `SURFACE` vs. command-scoped reads, and `accessibilityPlaceholderValue()` is repurposed as a fixture-only backdoor to assert the exact ARGV a pty was spawned with (`:1097-1100`) — a deliberate non-standard use of an AX property purely as a test seam.

## 4. Concurrency/async testing

Pure `async/await` dominates: **334 `func test...async` methods**, `@MainActor` appears in **67 test files**. `XCTestExpectation`/`expectation(description:)` is used sparingly — only **4 files** (`MarkdownFirstRenderTests`, `MarkdownRenderPipelineTests`, `RunCommandTests`, `WorkroomFileWatcherTests`), mostly for `NotificationCenter`/callback-driven async, not the default pattern.

Race/timing regressions are tested with the hand-rolled `settle()` run-loop-pumper (`WorkroomAppTests/Support/Settle.swift`):

```swift
// Support/Settle.swift:18-26
@MainActor
func settle(_ view: NSView, seconds: TimeInterval = 0.6, until condition: () -> Bool = { false }) {
  let deadline = Date().addingTimeInterval(seconds)
  while Date() < deadline {
    view.layoutSubtreeIfNeeded()
    RunLoop.current.run(until: Date().addingTimeInterval(0.02))
    if condition() { break }
  }
  view.layoutSubtreeIfNeeded()
}
```
This is a poll-until-condition-or-ceiling helper explicitly built for named app-hang regression suites (WORKROOM-2B/2T/2S per its doc comment) — a bespoke pattern rather than XCTest's native async facilities. No actor-gate/deterministic-clock abstraction was found; async timing races are tested against real `Task.sleep`/real clock with generous ceilings (e.g. `FixtureVCSWriter`'s 2.5s artificial delay so XCUITest's ~1s polling can observe an in-flight state — `UITestFixture.swift:1020-1026`).

## 5. External dependency isolation

**No fake git/jj backend for the write path** — `VCSCommitIntegrationTests.swift` and siblings (`VCSRemoteIntegrationTests`, `WorkroomStatusIntegrationTests`, `VCSProviderConformanceTests`, `GitGraphTests`) run the **real** `git`/`jj` binaries against **real ephemeral repos** under `NSTemporaryDirectory()`, cleaned up in `tearDown`:

```swift
// VCSCommitIntegrationTests.swift:39-43, 49-66
private func tempDir() -> String {
  let d = NSTemporaryDirectory() + "wr-commit-\(UUID().uuidString)"
  ...
}
private func sh(_ cmd: String, in dir: String) -> (out: String, exit: Int32) {
  ...
  env["GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL"] = "/dev/null"
  env["GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM"] = "/dev/null"
  env["GIT_AUTHOR_NAME"] = "T"; env["GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL"] = "t@e.com"
  ...
}
```
Isolation from the developer's machine is via explicit env vars (`GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null`, `GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM=/dev/null`, pinned author/committer identity, `PATH` forced through `ShellEnvironment.path()`), not a fake backend. The file's own doc comment states the rationale: unit-level argument builders "can only prove what we send"; this tier catches what git/jj actually *did* (4 real bugs cited inline). Faster unit tests instead inject `VCSProviding`/`StatusCommandRunning` stubs (§2) to avoid shelling out at all — so isolation strategy is bifurcated by tier (mocked-seam unit tests vs. real-binary integration tests), not a single fake-everywhere approach.

**UserDefaults isolation is notably *not* file-system/suite isolated.** There's no `UserDefaults(suiteName:)`, no `$HOME` override, no `MUXY_TEST`-style env var for unit tests. Instead, `AppStore` exposes targeted **override-for-testing properties** to route around the one real, shared "Workroom Dev" defaults domain that all parallel test workers share:

```swift
// AppStore.swift:520-527, 3645-3647
var isolatesInspectorLayoutForTesting = false
var isolatesInspectorSectionForTesting = false
...
var confirmOnCloseOverrideForTesting: Bool?
```
Comment at `AppStore.swift:522-526` explains the hazard directly: `-parallel-testing` gives each worker its own host process but **one on-disk UserDefaults domain**, so writing a shared key from one test worker leaks into another worker's store construction. The fix is per-property injected overrides, not env-var/HOME isolation — each hazardous setting needed its own bespoke seam, discovered incrementally (comments reference at least 4 of these: inspector layout, inspector section, inspector visibility, confirm-on-close).

UI-test isolation is separate and stronger: `UITestFixture` points at fresh temp directories (never `~/.config/workroom`) and gates session-file/agent-root paths default-off specifically so the ~30 UI tests can't clobber the developer's real session/`~/.claude`/`~/.codex` state (`UITestFixture.swift:62-85`).

## 6. Snapshot/visual testing

None. No `SnapshotTesting` (pointfreeco) or similar library in `project.yml`'s `packages:` block, and no `*.swift` references to image/view snapshot assertions. `JJSnapshotGateTests.swift` exists but tests an unrelated concept — jj's own working-copy "snapshot" (commit) mechanism, not visual regression testing. Visual/layout correctness is instead covered by the `settle()`-based layout-pump assertions (§4) and XCUITest accessibility-tree assertions (§3), not pixel/image comparison.

## 7. Test data/fixtures for git/jj/worktree scenarios

Two separate, both duplicated-per-file mechanisms:

- **Unit/integration tier**: ~20 files each hand-roll their own `tempDir()`/`gitRepo(files:)`/`jjRepo()` builders (no shared `RepoBuilder`). Example from `VCSCommitIntegrationTests.swift:78-83`:
```swift
private func gitRepo(files: [String: String] = ["base.txt": "base\n"]) -> String {
  let dir = tempDir()
  sh("git init -q . && git config user.email t@e.com && git config user.name T", in: dir)
  for (name, contents) in files { write(contents, to: name, in: dir) }
  sh("git add -A && git commit -qm base", in: dir)
  return dir
}
```
  `WorkroomStatusIntegrationTests.swift` separately defines its own `gitRepoWithUpstream()` (line 72) and `jjRepo()` (line 403) — none of these are shared across files despite near-identical shapes.
- **UI tier**: `UITestFixture.projects()` (`UITestFixture.swift:553-602`) is the single, well-centralized fixture builder for XCUITest — it creates real (but empty, non-VCS) temp directories under `NSTemporaryDirectory()/workroom-uitest/`, seeds a `Gemfile` and `NOTES.md` with marker strings for content assertions, and serves canned `VCSProviding`/`VCSWriting` data (`FixtureVCSProvider`, `FixtureVCSWriter`) rather than exercising real git/jj — deliberately, since the fixture's whole point is to avoid real VCS calls from the UI layer (`UITestFixture.swift:853-856`).

So: **XCUITest fixtures are centralized** (one `UITestFixture` enum); **unit/integration git/jj repo builders are not** (duplicated per file).

## 8. Framework

**100% XCTest.** `import XCTest` appears in 147 files; zero occurrences of `import Testing`, `@Test`, or `#expect(` anywhere in `WorkroomAppTests`/`WorkroomAppUITests`. This is fully consistent — no partial Swift Testing migration in progress. The Python supervisor test and shell-script tests are separate, framework-free (hand-rolled `check()`/assert-and-collect-failures patterns) tiers outside Xcode entirely.

## 9. CI/test scripts

`make app-test` (root `Makefile:90-91`) = `xcodegen generate` + `xcodebuild ... -parallel-testing-enabled YES test` against the `WorkroomApp` scheme's `WorkroomAppTests` target only. Parallelism is on by default (comment at `Makefile:52-57`: ~40% faster, 48s→~29s) but is a **known race source** — the same doc block that introduces it warns that a test mutating a shared `Defaults` key another parallel worker reads will race, which is exactly what §5's override-for-testing properties exist to route around.

- `make app-uitest` runs the separate `WorkroomAppUITests` scheme, and by default **skips 3 expensive/flaky UI tests** via `APP_UITEST_FLAGS` (`Makefile:60-67`) — `AgentResumeUITests`, `SessionRestoreUITests`, `HistoryStressUITests.testLargeHistoryStaysInteractive`, `WindowDragUITests.testDraggingWorkroomTabReordersTwoChips` — because "XCUITest never runs in CI" and routine local runs shouldn't pay 4-5 min for release-gating-only cases.
- CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:230-245`) runs exactly three test steps: `make app-test` (ad-hoc signed, since hosted runners have no dev cert/team), `make app-test-supervisor`, `make app-test-scripts` — **`make app-uitest` is never invoked in CI**, confirming the "UI tests don't run on GitHub CI" project memory. The build-helper/channel shell tests run separately in CI specifically because Debug-only single-arch `app-test` builds can't exercise the multi-arch packaging branch (`Scripts/build-helper_test.sh:11-13`).
- **No coverage gate anywhere** — no `-enableCodeCoverage`, no `xcresult`/coverage-percentage check in `Makefile`, `project.yml`, or `ci.yml`. Testing is gated purely on pass/fail, not on a coverage threshold.
- `make app-release` depends on `app-test-scripts` (cheap, catches artifact/arch bugs) but **deliberately not** on `app-test` itself (`Makefile:116` comment: `app-test` builds Debug, which pins a different arch/signing shape than the release artifact being shipped).

```swift
// WorkroomAppUITests/ActivityBarUITests.swift:13-20
private func launchedApp() -> XCUIApplication {
  let app = XCUIApplication()
  app.launchArguments += ["-WorkroomUITestFixture", "1"]
  app.launchArguments += ["-ApplePersistenceIgnoreState", "YES"]
  app.launch()
  app.activate()
  return app
}
```
33 of the 37 UI test files independently re-declare `launchedApp()`/`waitExists()` (confirmed by grep) — the same duplication pattern as the unit-test mocks, just for UI-test scaffolding instead of a shared XCUITest base class.

**Accessibility identifiers**: fixture-only ids, gated the same way, e.g. `activitySection.<rawValue>`, `inspector.header.<title>`, `sidebar.project.<name>`, `terminal.surface` (`GhosttySurfaceView.swift:1106-1108`: `override func accessibilityIdentifier() -> String { UITestFixture.isActive ? "terminal.surface" : super... }`).

**Terminal/Metal content assertion** — since libghostty renders through Metal with no text layer, `GhosttySurfaceView.swift` overrides `accessibilityValue()`/`accessibilitySelectedText()`/`accessibilityPlaceholderValue()` to expose `readText(tag: GHOSTTY_POINT_VIEWPORT)` (project memory's "fixture-only accessibilityValue pattern"), gated by:

```swift
// GhosttySurfaceView.swift:1060-1062
private var accessibilityContentEnabled: Bool {
  UITestFixture.isActive || NSWorkspace.shared.isVoiceOverEnabled
}
```
`readText(tag:)` (`GhosttySurfaceView.swift:845`) is the low-level libghostty read; `readFullSurface()` (`:866`) and `readCommandRegion(maxBytes:)` (`:822`) wrap it for `SURFACE` vs. command-scoped reads, and `accessibilityPlaceholderValue()` is repurposed as a fixture-only backdoor to assert the exact ARGV a pty was spawned with (`:1097-1100`) — a deliberate non-standard use of an AX property purely as a test seam.

## 4. Concurrency/async testing

Pure `async/await` dominates: **334 `func test...async` methods**, `@MainActor` appears in **67 test files**. `XCTestExpectation`/`expectation(description:)` is used sparingly — only **4 files** (`MarkdownFirstRenderTests`, `MarkdownRenderPipelineTests`, `RunCommandTests`, `WorkroomFileWatcherTests`), mostly for `NotificationCenter`/callback-driven async, not the default pattern.

Race/timing regressions are tested with the hand-rolled `settle()` run-loop-pumper (`WorkroomAppTests/Support/Settle.swift`):

```swift
// Support/Settle.swift:18-26
@MainActor
func settle(_ view: NSView, seconds: TimeInterval = 0.6, until condition: () -> Bool = { false }) {
  let deadline = Date().addingTimeInterval(seconds)
  while Date() < deadline {
    view.layoutSubtreeIfNeeded()
    RunLoop.current.run(until: Date().addingTimeInterval(0.02))
    if condition() { break }
  }
  view.layoutSubtreeIfNeeded()
}
```
This is a poll-until-condition-or-ceiling helper explicitly built for named app-hang regression suites (WORKROOM-2B/2T/2S per its doc comment) — a bespoke pattern rather than XCTest's native async facilities. No actor-gate/deterministic-clock abstraction was found; async timing races are tested against real `Task.sleep`/real clock with generous ceilings (e.g. `FixtureVCSWriter`'s 2.5s artificial delay so XCUITest's ~1s polling can observe an in-flight state — `UITestFixture.swift:1020-1026`).

## 5. External dependency isolation

**No fake git/jj backend for the write path** — `VCSCommitIntegrationTests.swift` and siblings (`VCSRemoteIntegrationTests`, `WorkroomStatusIntegrationTests`, `VCSProviderConformanceTests`, `GitGraphTests`) run the **real** `git`/`jj` binaries against **real ephemeral repos** under `NSTemporaryDirectory()`, cleaned up in `tearDown`:

```swift
// VCSCommitIntegrationTests.swift:39-43, 49-66
private func tempDir() -> String {
  let d = NSTemporaryDirectory() + "wr-commit-\(UUID().uuidString)"
  ...
}
private func sh(_ cmd: String, in dir: String) -> (out: String, exit: Int32) {
  ...
  env["GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL"] = "/dev/null"
  env["GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM"] = "/dev/null"
  env["GIT_AUTHOR_NAME"] = "T"; env["GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL"] = "t@e.com"
  ...
}
```
Isolation from the developer's machine is via explicit env vars (`GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null`, `GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM=/dev/null`, pinned author/committer identity, `PATH` forced through `ShellEnvironment.path()`), not a fake backend. The file's own doc comment states the rationale: unit-level argument builders "can only prove what we send"; this tier catches what git/jj actually *did* (4 real bugs cited inline). Faster unit tests instead inject `VCSProviding`/`StatusCommandRunning` stubs (§2) to avoid shelling out at all — so isolation strategy is bifurcated by tier (mocked-seam unit tests vs. real-binary integration tests), not a single fake-everywhere approach.

**UserDefaults isolation is notably *not* file-system/suite isolated.** There's no `UserDefaults(suiteName:)`, no `$HOME` override, no `MUXY_TEST`-style env var for unit tests. Instead, `AppStore` exposes targeted **override-for-testing properties** to route around the one real, shared "Workroom Dev" defaults domain that all parallel test workers share:

```swift
// AppStore.swift:520-527, 3645-3647
var isolatesInspectorLayoutForTesting = false
var isolatesInspectorSectionForTesting = false
...
var confirmOnCloseOverrideForTesting: Bool?
```
Comment at `AppStore.swift:522-526` explains the hazard directly: `-parallel-testing` gives each worker its own host process but **one on-disk UserDefaults domain**, so writing a shared key from one test worker leaks into another worker's store construction. The fix is per-property injected overrides, not env-var/HOME isolation — each hazardous setting needed its own bespoke seam, discovered incrementally (comments reference at least 4 of these: inspector layout, inspector section, inspector visibility, confirm-on-close).

UI-test isolation is separate and stronger: `UITestFixture` points at fresh temp directories (never `~/.config/workroom`) and gates session-file/agent-root paths default-off specifically so the ~30 UI tests can't clobber the developer's real session/`~/.claude`/`~/.codex` state (`UITestFixture.swift:62-85`).

## 6. Snapshot/visual testing

None. No `SnapshotTesting` (pointfreeco) or similar library in `project.yml`'s `packages:` block, and no `*.swift` references to image/view snapshot assertions. `JJSnapshotGateTests.swift` exists but tests an unrelated concept — jj's own working-copy "snapshot" (commit) mechanism, not visual regression testing. Visual/layout correctness is instead covered by the `settle()`-based layout-pump assertions (§4) and XCUITest accessibility-tree assertions (§3), not pixel/image comparison.

## 7. Test data/fixtures for git/jj/worktree scenarios

Two separate, both duplicated-per-file mechanisms:

- **Unit/integration tier**: ~20 files each hand-roll their own `tempDir()`/`gitRepo(files:)`/`jjRepo()` builders (no shared `RepoBuilder`). Example from `VCSCommitIntegrationTests.swift:78-83`:
```swift
private func gitRepo(files: [String: String] = ["base.txt": "base\n"]) -> String {
  let dir = tempDir()
  sh("git init -q . && git config user.email t@e.com && git config user.name T", in: dir)
  for (name, contents) in files { write(contents, to: name, in: dir) }
  sh("git add -A && git commit -qm base", in: dir)
  return dir
}
```
  `WorkroomStatusIntegrationTests.swift` separately defines its own `gitRepoWithUpstream()` (line 72) and `jjRepo()` (line 403) — none of these are shared across files despite near-identical shapes.
- **UI tier**: `UITestFixture.projects()` (`UITestFixture.swift:553-602`) is the single, well-centralized fixture builder for XCUITest — it creates real (but empty, non-VCS) temp directories under `NSTemporaryDirectory()/workroom-uitest/`, seeds a `Gemfile` and `NOTES.md` with marker strings for content assertions, and serves canned `VCSProviding`/`VCSWriting` data (`FixtureVCSProvider`, `FixtureVCSWriter`) rather than exercising real git/jj — deliberately, since the fixture's whole point is to avoid real VCS calls from the UI layer (`UITestFixture.swift:853-856`).

So: **XCUITest fixtures are centralized** (one `UITestFixture` enum); **unit/integration git/jj repo builders are not** (duplicated per file).

## 8. Framework

**100% XCTest.** `import XCTest` appears in 147 files; zero occurrences of `import Testing`, `@Test`, or `#expect(` anywhere in `WorkroomAppTests`/`WorkroomAppUITests`. This is fully consistent — no partial Swift Testing migration in progress. The Python supervisor test and shell-script tests are separate, framework-free (hand-rolled `check()`/assert-and-collect-failures patterns) tiers outside Xcode entirely.

## 9. CI/test scripts

`make app-test` (root `Makefile:90-91`) = `xcodegen generate` + `xcodebuild ... -parallel-testing-enabled YES test` against the `WorkroomApp` scheme's `WorkroomAppTests` target only. Parallelism is on by default (comment at `Makefile:52-57`: ~40% faster, 48s→~29s) but is a **known race source** — the same doc block that introduces it warns that a test mutating a shared `Defaults` key another parallel worker reads will race, which is exactly what §5's override-for-testing properties exist to route around.

- `make app-uitest` runs the separate `WorkroomAppUITests` scheme, and by default **skips 3 expensive/flaky UI tests** via `APP_UITEST_FLAGS` (`Makefile:60-67`) — `AgentResumeUITests`, `SessionRestoreUITests`, `HistoryStressUITests.testLargeHistoryStaysInteractive`, `WindowDragUITests.testDraggingWorkroomTabReordersTwoChips` — because "XCUITest never runs in CI" and routine local runs shouldn't pay 4-5 min for release-gating-only cases.
- CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:230-245`) runs exactly three test steps: `make app-test` (ad-hoc signed, since hosted runners have no dev cert/team), `make app-test-supervisor`, `make app-test-scripts` — **`make app-uitest` is never invoked in CI**, confirming the "UI tests don't run on GitHub CI" project memory. The build-helper/channel shell tests run separately in CI specifically because Debug-only single-arch `app-test` builds can't exercise the multi-arch packaging branch (`Scripts/build-helper_test.sh:11-13`).
- **No coverage gate anywhere** — no `-enableCodeCoverage`, no `xcresult`/coverage-percentage check in `Makefile`, `project.yml`, or `ci.yml`. Testing is gated purely on pass/fail, not on a coverage threshold.
- `make app-release` depends on `app-test-scripts` (cheap, catches artifact/arch bugs) but **deliberately not** on `app-test` itself (`Makefile:116` comment: `app-test` builds Debug, which pins a different arch/signing shape than the release artifact being shipped).

# Muxy vs Workroom test practices — findings

## Context

Joel asked for a review of how Muxy (`~/dev/muxy`, sibling ghostty-based Swift terminal app,
pulled to latest `origin/main` @ `03a6420`, 2026-08-12) implements its tests, to see what could
improve Workroom's macapp test suite. This is a findings-only writeup — no code changes.

Both projects are macOS/SwiftUI apps built on libghostty with git/VCS-heavy domains, which makes
the comparison unusually direct. Key framework difference up front: **Muxy is 100% Swift Testing
(`@Test`/`#expect`, 334 files, 3,297 tests); Workroom is 100% XCTest (147 files, 2,263 tests).**
No Swift Testing migration is proposed — at Workroom's scale that's a non-starter, and several
Muxy patterns below are trait-shaped (`.serialized`, `.timeLimit`, `@Test(arguments:)`) with no
clean XCTest equivalent, so they're named as XCTest-form translations or dropped, not copied.

## Adoptable patterns, ranked

### 1. Actor-gate pattern for deterministic concurrency tests — strongest, genuinely Muxy-derived

Muxy tests exact concurrency behavior (caps, coalescing, "last request wins") by injecting a
private `actor` that holds `CheckedContinuation`s and lets the test resolve them in a chosen
order — no `Task.sleep`, no timing flakiness. Reference: `GitRepositoryCheckCoordinatorTests.swift:148-211`
(`GitRepositoryCheckProbe` — `waitForActiveChecks(_:)` suspends until N concurrent calls are
in-flight, `releaseAll()` releases them, test asserts `maximumActiveCheckCount == 2`). The same
idiom recurs independently 11 times across Muxy's suite for different subsystems.

Workroom's equivalent today is `WorkroomAppTests/Support/Settle.swift` — a run-loop-pumping
poll-until-condition-or-ceiling helper (0.6s default) used by 7 files including named hang
regression suites. It's timing-based by construction: it works, but it proves "didn't happen
within N seconds," not "provably cannot happen."

This is worth adopting specifically because Workroom already has bug history in exactly this
class of race: the DiffViewer `.task` re-fire loop (memory: `macapp-diffviewer-task-refire-loop.md`),
the History-loads-forever GCD starvation (memory: `macapp-history-loads-forever-gcd.md`), and
`AppStoreDeleteRaceTests`. An actor-gate test on any of these would assert the invariant
directly (e.g. "at most one load in flight for a given file key") instead of asserting "settled
within 0.6s," and would fail deterministically rather than flake under load.

### 2. `NSHostingView` + `layoutSubtreeIfNeeded()` + `fittingSize` — closes a real CI gap

Muxy tests SwiftUI layout behavior without XCUITest and without snapshot testing: build the real
view via `NSHostingView(rootView:)`, force layout, assert on `fittingSize`/subview structure.
Reference: `ExtensionConsentDialogTests.swift:36-51`.

The reason this matters for Workroom isn't "lighter than XCUITest" in the abstract — it's a
concrete CI asymmetry already on record: `.github/workflows/ci.yml:230-245` runs `make app-test`
but never `make app-uitest` ("UI tests don't run on GitHub CI" per project memory). Any
layout/structure assertion written as an `NSHostingView` unit test runs in the tier CI actually
executes on every push; the same assertion as an XCUITest only runs when someone remembers to
run it locally. This moves coverage from never-verified-on-CI to verified-on-every-push for
SwiftUI views that don't need a live window or real terminal content.

Not a replacement for Workroom's XCUITest tier — Workroom's fixture/accessibility-based terminal
content assertions (`readText`, `GhosttySurfaceView` accessibility overrides) have no Muxy
equivalent at all (Muxy has zero XCUITest, by explicit "never run the app" policy) and are more
sophisticated than anything in Muxy. This technique is a narrow, useful addition for pure-SwiftUI
layout checks specifically.

### 3. Meta-test guarding your own scripts

Muxy has `TestIsolationScriptTests.swift:43-51` — a test that reads `scripts/checks.sh`'s source
as text and asserts it still invokes the test-isolation wrapper, guarding against someone
silently removing it. Pure string-read-and-assert, zero framework friction, trivial to port to
XCTest.

Workroom has comparably fragile invariants living only in `Makefile` comments today: the
`APP_UITEST_FLAGS` skip list (3 UI tests skipped by default per `Makefile:60-67`), CI's
`make app-test-scripts` invocation, and `app-release` deliberately *not* depending on `app-test`
(`Makefile:116`). A small test class that greps `Makefile`/`ci.yml` for these strings would catch
someone accidentally dropping one during a refactor, the same way Muxy's does.

### 4. `XCTSkip` for build-artifact-dependent tests

Muxy's session-daemon E2E tests use `.enabled(if: SessionDaemonHarness.binaryURL != nil)` to skip
gracefully — rather than fail — when a debug binary they depend on hasn't been built. The direct
XCTest translation is `throw XCTSkip(...)` at the top of the test. Relevant if Workroom's
`run-supervisor` Python tests or any future test depends on a built CLI/helper binary being
present; worth keeping in mind rather than failing hard or silently no-op'ing.

## Real duplication found in both — not "Muxy learnings," found while comparing

These three gaps exist in **both** codebases. Muxy does not do them well either (see specifics
below), so they're not "adopt Muxy's approach" — they're independently-confirmed opportunities
Workroom could get right where Muxy hasn't:

- **Shared VCS test-double module.** Workroom re-implements `VCSProviding`/`StatusCommandRunning`/
  `VCSWriting` stubs privately in ~10 files (`BranchResolverTests.swift:7` `StubProvider`,
  `HistoryModelTests.swift:18` `FakeProvider`, `WorkroomStatusResolverTests.swift:7`
  `MockStatusRunner`, etc.) with no shared `Fakes.swift`. Muxy has the same problem — its
  `Support/` folder exists but doesn't consolidate the analogous `TempGitRepo`/`StubURLProtocol`
  duplication (3 independent `TempGitRepo` copies, `StubURLProtocol` duplicated in 3 files, 11
  files with private `makeTempDir()`).
- **Shared git/jj repo fixture builder.** ~20 Workroom files each hand-roll `tempDir()`/
  `gitRepo(files:)`/`jjRepo()` (e.g. `VCSCommitIntegrationTests.swift:78-83`,
  `WorkroomStatusIntegrationTests.swift` separately defining `gitRepoWithUpstream()` and
  `jjRepo()`). Muxy's XCUITest-equivalent problem is identical in shape.
- **Shared XCUITest launch/wait helpers.** 33 of Workroom's 37 UI test files independently
  redeclare `launchedApp()`/`waitExists()`. N/A comparison to Muxy (no XCUITest there), but it's
  the same duplication shape as the two items above and worth fixing in the same pass if ever
  addressed.

## Considered and declined

- **Coverage gate** (Muxy: `MIN_LINE_COVERAGE=90` via `xcrun llvm-cov report`, opt-in, scoped to
  Models/parsers). Not recommended. Muxy's own gate visibly produced `ModelCoverageTests.swift` —
  a `.serialized` grab-bag suite stitching ~12 unrelated small assertions together, which the
  survey flags as a coverage-driven anti-pattern, not a model to import.
- **Global test-process detection to auto-isolate storage** (Muxy: `MuxyFileStorage.isTestProcess`
  redirects Application Support JSON persistence via `MUXY_TEST_APPLICATION_SUPPORT_DIRECTORY`).
  Investigated and rejected for Workroom specifically:
  - Muxy's mechanism only covers its JSON file persistence layer — it does *not* solve
    UserDefaults isolation globally either; Muxy still hand-rolls `UserDefaults(suiteName:
    "...-\(UUID())")` independently in 22 files, the same per-site pattern Workroom already has.
  - Workroom's actual hazard is `Defaults`-backed keys (sindresorhus/Defaults) sharing one real
    on-disk UserDefaults domain across parallel test workers (per-process `$HOME`/env overrides
    don't touch it — cfprefsd resolves the real home regardless, per memory
    `userdefaults-not-isolated-by-home.md`).
  - Workroom already made a deliberate, documented architectural call here:
    `WorkroomAppTests/SharedPrefDefaultsTests.swift` explains in detail why per-property
    `...ForTesting` override flags on `AppStore` (not blanket isolation) were chosen — ~47
    production call sites branch on the real fixture/prefs keys, so auto-isolating everything
    when a test process is detected would silently change behavior those sites depend on. The
    single-writer-class discipline for raw key writes, and per-property overrides for everything
    else, is already the considered-correct answer to the exact problem Muxy's mechanism targets.
  - Verified before writing this off: 282 of 389 `Defaults.Key` declarations already scope to an
    explicit `suite:`, and multiple existing tests (`SharedPrefDefaultsTests`, `RunCommandTests`,
    `ConfirmOnCloseTerminalTests`, etc.) rely on specific `ForTesting` flags being off by default.
    Nothing to change here.

## Bottom line

Three things worth doing if/when Joel wants to act on this: an actor-gate-style deterministic
concurrency test for one of the known race-prone subsystems (item 1), an `NSHostingView` layout
test for a SwiftUI view that currently only has XCUITest coverage (item 2, closes the CI gap),
and a small meta-test pinning the `Makefile`/CI invariants (item 3). The duplication cleanups
(shared fakes, shared repo builders, shared XCUITest helpers) are good chores but are
independent of the Muxy comparison — Muxy hasn't solved them either.

This plan is findings-only per Joel's answer — no implementation follows from this session.

## AskUserQuestion Format

### Tool resolution (read first)

"AskUserQuestion" can resolve to two tools at runtime: the **host MCP variant** (e.g. `mcp__conductor__AskUserQuestion` — appears in your tool list when the host registers it) or the **native** Claude Code tool.

**Conductor rule (read before the MCP rule):** if `CONDUCTOR_SESSION: true` was echoed by the preamble, do NOT call AskUserQuestion at all — neither native nor any `mcp__*__AskUserQuestion` variant. Render EVERY decision brief as the **prose form** below and STOP. This is proactive, not a reaction to a failure: Conductor disables native AUQ and its MCP variant is flaky (it returns `[Tool result missing due to internal error]`), so prose is the reliable path. **Auto-decide preferences still apply first:** if a `[plan-tune auto-decide] <id> → <option>` result has already surfaced for a question, proceed with that option (no prose). Because in Conductor you go straight to prose without ever calling the tool, this auto-decide-first ordering is enforced HERE, not only by the PreToolUse hook. When you render a Conductor prose brief, also capture it with `bin/gstack-question-log` (the PostToolUse capture hook never fires on a prose path, so `/plan-tune` history/learning depends on this call).

**Rule (non-Conductor):** if any `mcp__*__AskUserQuestion` variant is in your tool list, prefer it. Hosts may disable native AUQ via `--disallowedTools AskUserQuestion` (Conductor does, by default) and route through their MCP variant; calling native there silently fails. Same questions/options shape; same decision-brief format applies.

If AskUserQuestion is unavailable (no variant in your tool list) OR a call to it fails, do NOT silently auto-decide or write the decision to the plan file as a substitute. Follow the **failure fallback** below.

### When AskUserQuestion is unavailable or a call fails

Tell three outcomes apart:

1. **Auto-decide denial (NOT a failure).** The result contains `[plan-tune auto-decide] <id> → <option>` — the preference hook working as designed. Proceed with that option. Do NOT retry, do NOT fall back to prose.
2. **Genuine failure** — no variant in your tool list, OR the variant is present but the call returns an error / missing result (MCP transport error, empty result, host bug — e.g. Conductor's MCP AskUserQuestion is flaky and returns `[Tool result missing due to internal error]`).
   - If it was present and **errored** (not absent), retry the SAME call **once** — but only if no answer could have surfaced (a missing-result error can arrive after the user already saw the question; retrying would double-prompt, so if it may have reached them, treat as pending, don't retry).
   - Then branch on `SESSION_KIND` (echoed by the preamble; empty/absent ⇒ `interactive`):
     - `spawned` → defer to the **Spawned session** block: auto-choose the recommended option. Never prose, never BLOCKED.
     - `headless` → `BLOCKED — AskUserQuestion unavailable`; stop and wait (no human can answer).
     - `interactive` → **prose fallback** (below).

**Prose fallback — render the decision brief as a markdown message, not a tool call.** Same information as the tool format below, different structure (paragraphs, not ✅/❌ bullets). It MUST surface this triad:

1. **A clear ELI10 of the issue itself** — plain English on what's being decided and why it matters (the question, not per-choice), naming the stakes. Lead with it.
2. **Completeness scores per choice** — explicit `Completeness: X/10` on EACH choice (10 complete, 7 happy-path, 3 shortcut); use the kind-note when options differ in kind not coverage, but never silently drop the score.
3. **The recommendation and why** — a `Recommendation: <choice> because <reason>` line plus the `(recommended)` marker on that choice.

Layout: a `D<N>` title + a one-line note to reply with a letter (in Conductor this is the normal path; elsewhere it means AskUserQuestion was unavailable or errored); the issue ELI10; the Recommendation line; then ONE paragraph per choice carrying its `(recommended)` marker, its `Completeness: X/10`, and 2-4 sentences of reasoning — never a bare bullet list; a closing `Net:` line. Split chains / 5+ options: one prose block per per-option call, in sequence. Then STOP and wait — the user's typed answer is the decision. In plan mode this satisfies end-of-turn like a tool call.

**Continuation — mapping a typed reply back to a brief.** Each brief carries a stable label (`D<N>`, or `D<N>.k` in a split chain). The user references it (e.g. "3.2: B"). A bare letter maps to the single most-recent UNANSWERED brief; if more than one is open (a split chain), do NOT guess — ask which `D<N>.k` it answers. Never apply a bare letter ambiguously across a chain.

**One-way / destructive confirmations in prose.** When the decision is a one-way door (irreversible or destructive — delete, force-push, drop, overwrite), prose is a WEAKER gate than the tool, so make it stronger: require an explicit typed confirmation (the exact option letter or word), state plainly what is irreversible, and NEVER proceed on a vague, partial, or ambiguous reply — re-ask instead. Treat silence or "ok"/"sure" without the explicit choice as not-yet-confirmed.

### Format

Every AskUserQuestion is a decision brief and must be sent as tool_use, not prose — unless the documented failure fallback above applies (interactive session + the call is unavailable/erroring), in which case the prose fallback is the correct output.

```
D<N> — <one-line question title>
Project/branch/task: <1 short grounding sentence using _BRANCH>
ELI10: <plain English a 16-year-old could follow, 2-4 sentences, name the stakes>
Stakes if we pick wrong: <one sentence on what breaks, what user sees, what's lost>
Recommendation: <choice> because <one-line reason>
Completeness: A=X/10, B=Y/10   (or: Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score)
Pros / cons:
A) <option label> (recommended)
  ✅ <pro — concrete, observable, ≥40 chars>
  ❌ <con — honest, ≥40 chars>
B) <option label>
  ✅ <pro>
  ❌ <con>
Net: <one-line synthesis of what you're actually trading off>
```

D-numbering: first question in a skill invocation is `D1`; increment yourself. This is a model-level instruction, not a runtime counter.

ELI10 is always present, in plain English, not function names. Recommendation is ALWAYS present. Keep the `(recommended)` label; AUTO_DECIDE depends on it.

Completeness: use `Completeness: N/10` only when options differ in coverage. 10 = complete, 7 = happy path, 3 = shortcut. If options differ in kind, write: `Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score.`

Pros / cons: use ✅ and ❌. Minimum 2 pros and 1 con per option when the choice is real; Minimum 40 characters per bullet. Hard-stop escape for one-way/destructive confirmations: `✅ No cons — this is a hard-stop choice`.

Neutral posture: `Recommendation: <default> — this is a taste call, no strong preference either way`; `(recommended)` STAYS on the default option for AUTO_DECIDE.

Effort both-scales: when an option involves effort, label both human-team and CC+gstack time, e.g. `(human: ~2 days / CC: ~15 min)`. Makes AI compression visible at decision time.

Net line closes the tradeoff. Per-skill instructions may add stricter rules.

### Handling 5+ options — split, never drop

AskUserQuestion caps every call at **4 options**. With 5+ real options, NEVER
drop, merge, or silently defer one to fit. Pick a compliant shape:

- **Batch into ≤4-groups** — for coherent alternatives (e.g. version bumps,
  layout variants). One call, 5th surfaced only if first 4 don't fit.
- **Split per-option** — for independent scope items (e.g. "ship E1..E6?").
  Fire N sequential calls, one per option. Default to this when unsure.

Per-option call shape: `D<N>.k` header (e.g. D3.1..D3.5), ELI10 per option,
Recommendation, kind-note (no completeness score — Include/Defer/Cut/Hold are
decision actions), and 4 buckets:
**A) Include**, **B) Defer**, **C) Cut**, **D) Hold** (stop chain, discuss).

After the chain, fire `D<N>.final` to validate the assembled set (reprompt
dependency conflicts) and confirm shipping it. Use `D<N>.revise-<k>` to
revise one option without re-running the chain.

For N>6, fire a `D<N>.0` meta-AskUserQuestion first (proceed / narrow / batch).

question_ids for split chains: `<skill>-split-<option-slug>` (kebab-case ASCII,
≤64 chars, `-2`/`-3` suffix on collision). The runtime checker
(`bin/gstack-question-preference`) refuses `never-ask` on any `*-split-*` id,
so split chains are never AUTO_DECIDE-eligible — the user's option set is sacred.

**Full rule + worked examples + Hold/dependency semantics:** see
`docs/askuserquestion-split.md` in the gstack repo. Read on demand when N>4.

**Non-ASCII characters — write directly, never \u-escape.** When any string
field contains Chinese (繁體/簡體), Japanese, Korean, or other non-ASCII text,
emit the literal UTF-8 characters; never escape them as `\uXXXX` (the pipe is
UTF-8 native, and manual escaping miscodes long CJK strings). Only `\n`,
`\t`, `\"`, `\\` remain allowed. Full rationale + worked example: see
`docs/askuserquestion-cjk.md`. Read on demand when a question contains CJK.

### Self-check before emitting

Before calling AskUserQuestion, verify:
- [ ] D<N> header present
- [ ] ELI10 paragraph present (stakes line too)
- [ ] Recommendation line present with concrete reason
- [ ] Completeness scored (coverage) OR kind-note present (kind)
- [ ] Every option has ≥2 ✅ and ≥1 ❌, each ≥40 chars (or hard-stop escape)
- [ ] (recommended) label on one option (even for neutral-posture)
- [ ] Dual-scale effort labels on effort-bearing options (human / CC)
- [ ] Net line closes the decision
- [ ] You are calling the tool, not writing prose — unless `CONDUCTOR_SESSION: true` (then prose is the DEFAULT, not the tool) OR the documented failure fallback applies (then: prose with the mandatory triad — issue ELI10, per-choice Completeness, Recommendation + `(recommended)` — and a "reply with a letter" instruction, then STOP)
- [ ] Non-ASCII characters (CJK / accents) written directly, NOT \u-escaped
- [ ] If you had 5+ options, you split (or batched into ≤4-groups) — did NOT drop any
- [ ] If you split, you checked dependencies between options before firing the chain
- [ ] If a per-option Hold fires, you stopped the chain immediately (didn't queue)


## Artifacts Sync (skill start)

```bash
_GSTACK_HOME="${GSTACK_HOME:-$HOME/.gstack}"
# Prefer the v1.27.0.0 artifacts file; fall back to brain file for users
# upgrading mid-stream before the migration script runs.
if [ -f "$HOME/.gstack-artifacts-remote.txt" ]; then
  _BRAIN_REMOTE_FILE="$HOME/.gstack-artifacts-remote.txt"
else
  _BRAIN_REMOTE_FILE="$HOME/.gstack-brain-remote.txt"
fi
_BRAIN_SYNC_BIN="~/.claude/skills/gstack/bin/gstack-brain-sync"
_BRAIN_CONFIG_BIN="~/.claude/skills/gstack/bin/gstack-config"

# /sync-gbrain context-load: teach the agent to use gbrain when it's available.
# Per-worktree pin: post-spike redesign uses kubectl-style `.gbrain-source` in the
# git toplevel to scope queries. Look for the pin in the worktree (not a global
# state file) so that opening worktree B without a pin doesn't claim "indexed"
# just because worktree A was synced. Empty string when gbrain is not
# configured (zero context cost for non-gbrain users).
_GBRAIN_CONFIG="$HOME/.gbrain/config.json"
if [ -f "$_GBRAIN_CONFIG" ] && command -v gbrain >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  _GBRAIN_VERSION_OK=$(gbrain --version 2>/dev/null | grep -c '^gbrain ' || echo 0)
  if [ "$_GBRAIN_VERSION_OK" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then
    _GBRAIN_PIN_PATH=""
    _REPO_TOP=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || echo "")
    if [ -n "$_REPO_TOP" ] && [ -f "$_REPO_TOP/.gbrain-source" ]; then
      _GBRAIN_PIN_PATH="$_REPO_TOP/.gbrain-source"
    fi
    if [ -n "$_GBRAIN_PIN_PATH" ]; then
      echo "GBrain configured. Prefer \`gbrain search\`/\`gbrain query\` over Grep for"
      echo "semantic questions; use \`gbrain code-def\`/\`code-refs\`/\`code-callers\` for"
      echo "symbol-aware code lookup. See \"## GBrain Search Guidance\" in CLAUDE.md."
      echo "Run /sync-gbrain to refresh."
    else
      echo "GBrain configured but this worktree isn't pinned yet. Run \`/sync-gbrain --full\`"
      echo "before relying on \`gbrain search\` for code questions in this worktree."
      echo "Falls back to Grep until pinned."
    fi
  fi
fi

_BRAIN_SYNC_MODE=$("$_BRAIN_CONFIG_BIN" get artifacts_sync_mode 2>/dev/null || echo off)

# Detect remote-MCP mode (Path 4 of /setup-gbrain). Local artifacts sync is
# a no-op in remote mode; the brain server pulls from GitHub/GitLab on its
# own cadence. Read claude.json directly to keep this preamble fast (no
# subprocess to claude CLI on every skill start).
_GBRAIN_MCP_MODE="none"
if command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ -f "$HOME/.claude.json" ]; then
  _GBRAIN_MCP_TYPE=$(jq -r '.mcpServers.gbrain.type // .mcpServers.gbrain.transport // empty' "$HOME/.claude.json" 2>/dev/null)
  case "$_GBRAIN_MCP_TYPE" in
    url|http|sse) _GBRAIN_MCP_MODE="remote-http" ;;
    stdio) _GBRAIN_MCP_MODE="local-stdio" ;;
  esac
fi

if [ -f "$_BRAIN_REMOTE_FILE" ] && [ ! -d "$_GSTACK_HOME/.git" ] && [ "$_BRAIN_SYNC_MODE" = "off" ]; then
  _BRAIN_NEW_URL=$(head -1 "$_BRAIN_REMOTE_FILE" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '[:space:]')
  if [ -n "$_BRAIN_NEW_URL" ]; then
    echo "ARTIFACTS_SYNC: artifacts repo detected: $_BRAIN_NEW_URL"
    echo "ARTIFACTS_SYNC: run 'gstack-brain-restore' to pull your cross-machine artifacts (or 'gstack-config set artifacts_sync_mode off' to dismiss forever)"
  fi
fi

if [ -d "$_GSTACK_HOME/.git" ] && [ "$_BRAIN_SYNC_MODE" != "off" ]; then
  _BRAIN_LAST_PULL_FILE="$_GSTACK_HOME/.brain-last-pull"
  _BRAIN_NOW=$(date +%s)
  _BRAIN_DO_PULL=1
  if [ -f "$_BRAIN_LAST_PULL_FILE" ]; then
    _BRAIN_LAST=$(cat "$_BRAIN_LAST_PULL_FILE" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
    _BRAIN_AGE=$(( _BRAIN_NOW - _BRAIN_LAST ))
    [ "$_BRAIN_AGE" -lt 86400 ] && _BRAIN_DO_PULL=0
  fi
  if [ "$_BRAIN_DO_PULL" = "1" ]; then
    ( cd "$_GSTACK_HOME" && git fetch origin >/dev/null 2>&1 && git merge --ff-only "origin/$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)" >/dev/null 2>&1 ) || true
    echo "$_BRAIN_NOW" > "$_BRAIN_LAST_PULL_FILE"
  fi
  "$_BRAIN_SYNC_BIN" --once 2>/dev/null || true
fi

if [ "$_GBRAIN_MCP_MODE" = "remote-http" ]; then
  # Remote-MCP mode: local artifacts sync is a no-op (brain admin's server
  # pulls from GitHub/GitLab). Show the user this is by design, not broken.
  _GBRAIN_HOST=$(jq -r '.mcpServers.gbrain.url // empty' "$HOME/.claude.json" 2>/dev/null | sed -E 's|^https?://([^/:]+).*|\1|')
  echo "ARTIFACTS_SYNC: remote-mode (managed by brain server ${_GBRAIN_HOST:-remote})"
elif [ -d "$_GSTACK_HOME/.git" ] && [ "$_BRAIN_SYNC_MODE" != "off" ]; then
  _BRAIN_QUEUE_DEPTH=0
  [ -f "$_GSTACK_HOME/.brain-queue.jsonl" ] && _BRAIN_QUEUE_DEPTH=$(wc -l < "$_GSTACK_HOME/.brain-queue.jsonl" | tr -d ' ')
  _BRAIN_LAST_PUSH="never"
  [ -f "$_GSTACK_HOME/.brain-last-push" ] && _BRAIN_LAST_PUSH=$(cat "$_GSTACK_HOME/.brain-last-push" 2>/dev/null || echo never)
  echo "ARTIFACTS_SYNC: mode=$_BRAIN_SYNC_MODE | last_push=$_BRAIN_LAST_PUSH | queue=$_BRAIN_QUEUE_DEPTH"
else
  echo "ARTIFACTS_SYNC: off"
fi
```

## Model-Specific Behavioral Patch (claude)

The following nudges are tuned for the claude model family. They are
**subordinate** to skill workflow, STOP points, AskUserQuestion gates, plan-mode
safety, and /ship review gates. If a nudge below conflicts with skill instructions,
the skill wins. Treat these as preferences, not rules.

**Todo-list discipline.** When working through a multi-step plan, mark each task
complete individually as you finish it. Do not batch-complete at the end. If a task
turns out to be unnecessary, mark it skipped with a one-line reason.

**Think before heavy actions.** For complex operations (refactors, migrations,
non-trivial new features), briefly state your approach before executing. This lets
the user course-correct cheaply instead of mid-flight.

**Dedicated tools over Bash.** Prefer Read, Edit, Write, Glob, Grep over shell
equivalents (cat, sed, find, grep). The dedicated tools are cheaper and clearer.

## Voice

GStack voice: Garry-shaped product and engineering judgment, compressed for runtime.

- Lead with the point. Say what it does, why it matters, and what changes for the builder.
- Be concrete. Name files, functions, line numbers, commands, outputs, evals, and real numbers.
- Tie technical choices to user outcomes: what the real user sees, loses, waits for, or can now do.
- Be direct about quality. Bugs matter. Edge cases matter. Fix the whole thing, not the demo path.
- Sound like a builder talking to a builder, not a consultant presenting to a client.
- Never corporate, academic, PR, or hype. Avoid filler, throat-clearing, generic optimism, and founder cosplay.
- No em dashes. No AI vocabulary: delve, crucial, robust, comprehensive, nuanced, multifaceted, furthermore, moreover, additionally, pivotal, landscape, tapestry, underscore, foster, showcase, intricate, vibrant, fundamental, significant.
- The user has context you do not: domain knowledge, timing, relationships, taste. Cross-model agreement is a recommendation, not a decision. The user decides.

Good: "auth.ts:47 returns undefined when the session cookie expires. Users hit a white screen. Fix: add a null check and redirect to /login. Two lines."
Bad: "I've identified a potential issue in the authentication flow that may cause problems under certain conditions."

## Completeness Principle — Boil the Ocean

AI makes completeness cheap, so the complete thing is the goal. Recommend full coverage (tests, edge cases, error paths) — boil the ocean one lake at a time. The only thing out of scope is genuinely unrelated work (rewrites, multi-quarter migrations); flag that as separate scope, never as an excuse for a shortcut.

When options differ in coverage, include `Completeness: X/10` (10 = all edge cases, 7 = happy path, 3 = shortcut). When options differ in kind, write: `Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score.` Do not fabricate scores.

## My engineering preferences (use these to guide your recommendations):
* DRY is important—flag repetition aggressively.
